qdc_qhc_relationship.summary: Part 1, s1.6, Table 1.6.1 of the MBRC Planning Scheme expressly identifies 'Alternative provisions to QDC boundary clearance and site cover provisions for a dwelling house, including a class 10 building or structure (Building Act 1975 section 33)' as located in s6.2.10 Rural zone code, s6.2.11 Rural residential zone code and s9.3.1 Dwelling house code, limited to 'RADs and performance outcomes identified by notes as a planning scheme matter'. In the Dwelling house code (9.3.1), most Part A RADs (RAD1-RAD6, RAD8-RAD14, RAD16-RAD25, plus RAD7 where not a Class 10 building) carry the note 'Non-compliance with this RAD is a planning scheme matter for which Council will exercise a concurrence agency role ...' - these are the provisions Table 1.6.1 identifies as alternative provisions (setbacks RAD3, built-to-boundary walls RAD4, site cover RAD5, height RAD1/RAD2, etc.). RAD7 (for a Class 10 building), RAD15 (earthworks) and RAD26 (domestic outbuildings) are declared 'amenity and aesthetic impact' matters (also concurrence). Values-and-constraints (overlay) RADs (RAD27 onward) carry neither note; non-compliance makes the work code assessable (limited assessment under 5.3.3.1.a.ii). In the Rural residential zone code (6.2.11), the 'Concurrence agency issues for building work' table lists RAD6 (roofed area/site cover), RAD8, RAD47 (height), RAD48 (setbacks) and RAD50 under 'Alternative provisions to the QDC', and 'Nil' under amenity/aesthetics. RAD6 and RAD48 also carry notes naming the QDC MP1.2 acceptable solutions they replace. The dwelling house code setback tables still say 'Refer to standard as in QDC' for side/rear setbacks in most precincts, and say 'The calculation for mean height is defined in the QDC'. No reference to the Queensland Housing Code (QHC) was found in any Version 8 text fetched (Part 1, Part 5 tables, 9.3.1, 6.2.6, 6.2.11, local plan and overlay codes), and the council's Dwelling house info sheet does not mention it. So as at Version 8 (11 Sep 2026) the scheme had NOT been amended to refer to the QHC. How the scheme's references to 'QDC part MP1.2' / 'standard as in QDC' operate after the QHC replaced MP1.1/MP1.2 on 1 Sep 2026 depends on Building Act / Building Regulation transitional provisions and is not resolved here.

definitions.text: For a building or structure, the shortest distance measured horizontally from the outer most projection of a building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot.

The outermost projection of any part of a building or structure including, in the case of a roof, the outside face of the fascia, or the roof structure where there is no fascia, or attached sunhoods or the like, but does not include retractable blinds, fixed screens, rainwater fittings, or ornamental attachments.

The proportion of the site covered by a building(s), structure(s) attached to the building(s) and carport(s), calculated to the outer most projections of the building(s) and expressed as a percentage. The term does not include: - any structure or part thereof included in a landscaped open space area such as a gazebo or shade structure; - basement car parking areas located wholly below ground level; and - eaves and sun shading devices.

If specified: - in metres, the vertical distance between the ground level and the highest point of the building roof (apex) or parapet at any point, but not including load-bearing antenna, aerial, chimney, flagpole or the like; - in storeys, the number of storeys above ground level; or - in both metres and storeys, both (a) and (b) apply. Editor's note - Lift overruns, air conditioners and the like, are excluded from the measure of building height.
The level of the natural ground, or, where the level of the natural ground has been changed, the level as lawfully changed.

A space that is situated between one floor level and the floor level next above, or if there is no floor above, the ceiling or roof above, but not a space that contains only: - a lift shaft, stairway or meter room - a bathroom, shower room, laundry, water closet, or other sanitary compartment - a combination of the above. A mezzanine is a storey. A roofed structure on or part of a rooftop that does not solely accommodate building plant and equipment is a storey. A basement is not a storey.

A Class 10a building, as defined in the Building Code of Australia , that is ancillary to a residential use on the same premises and is limited to non-habitable buildings for the purpose of a shed, garage and carport. Editor's note - This term includes 'and the like' buildings or roofed structures. Editor's note - This term is a building or other roofed structure that is detached from the dwelling. It is solely a class 10a and does not incorporate a component of any other class. Further, Domestic outbuildings are not garages and carports constructed to appear as an integral part of a dwelling (e.g. a single roof over the dwelling and garage parts of a building) and where the roof of a carport is attached directly to a dwelling (i.e. not attached via an ancillary structure such as a roofed walkway or pergola etc.)

Dwelling house means a residential use of premises involving - 1 dwelling and any domestic outbuildings associated with the dwelling; or - 2 dwellings, 1 of which is a secondary dwelling, and any domestic outbuildings associated with either dwelling.
* Any boundary line, or part thereof, of a lot which abuts a road reserve.

* Means: - for a lot with only one frontage to a road, the frontage to that road; or - for a lot with more than one frontage to a road (including a corner lot); - if the lot has a frontage to a laneway as described in Planning Scheme Policy Neighbourhood Design, the non-laneway frontage; and - if the frontages are to roads of a different order (as shown on the Overlap Map - Road Hierarchy) and excluding a motorway, the highest order road; and - if the frontages are to roads of the same order (as shown on the Overlap Map - Road Hierarchy): - the road that existing development on the land proposed to remain has, or is required to have, its principal pedestrian entrance into the development from (generally in the form of a front door); or - where (A.) does not apply; the road that development on adjoining land (having the same multiple road frontages) has or is required to have its principal pedestrian entrance into the development from (generally in the form of a front door); or - where (A.) and (B.) do not apply, the frontage the development is required to have or will have its principal pedestrian entrance into the development from (generally in the form of a front door). ...
* A frontage that is not the primary frontage.
* The line extending from the longest wall excluding a garage, carport or other domestic outbuilding in the front elevation of the building. Note - Excludes porticos, etc Figure - Main building line
* A wall of a Dwelling house (class 1a) setback 200mm or less from a boundary.
* The area of the roof of each building or other structure as projected onto a horizontal plane.

* A body of water, whether natural, constructed or artificially improved, which is ordinarily of sufficient size and depth to allow use by any occupied, motorised vessel. The term includes a canal, lake, river or stream, regardless of its salinity level and whether or not it is subject to tidal influence. However, the term specifically excludes any dam which is fully contained within a single lot, wastewater ponds, tailings dams and any other body of water to which entry by the public for motorised boating purposes is not permitted.

* A lot that is provided with infrastructure and services (including reticulated water and sewer, stormwater, dedicated roads and electricity) of a standard and capacity required for the proposed development.

* A plan approved by Council (generally as part of a reconfiguring a lot application) that regulates building elements (e.g. Built to boundary walls, driveway location etc) for development on narrow lots (generally lots with a frontage of 12.5m or less).

The total floor area of all storeys of a building (measured from the outside of the external walls or the centre of a common wall), other than areas used for the following: - building services, plant and equipment; - access between levels; - ground floor public lobby; - a mall; - the parking, loading and manoeuvring of motor vehicles; - unenclosed private balconies whether roofed or not.

local_plan_mechanism.summary: Local plans (Part 7: Redcliffe Kippa-Ring, Woodfordia, Caboolture West) have their own tables of assessment in 5.9 that replace the zone tables where they apply (5.3.1/5.3.2), and their codes prevail over zone and use codes to the extent of inconsistency (1.5). For dwelling houses, the local plan table either points to the 9.3.1 Dwelling house code (Redcliffe Interim residential precinct, Caboolture West Urban living - Next generation sub-precinct, which 9.3.1 RAD3/RAD5 route to particular setback/site cover tables) or adds the local plan code as a further benchmark. There are no separate 'neighbourhood plans' in this scheme; zone precincts act as the main variation layer.

open_questions: QHC transition: the scheme (Version 8, 11 Sep 2026) still refers to 'QDC part MP1.2' and 'standard as in QDC'. No QHC amendment was found. Confirm how Building Act/Regulation transitional provisions apply these references after the QHC commenced on 1 Sep 2026, especially the side/rear cells that say 'Refer to standard as in QDC' and the QDC mean-height method.

Alternative provisions in 9.3.1 are identified indirectly (Table 1.6.1 plus 'planning scheme matter' notes), not by an explicit 'alternative provision to QDC A1...' statement per RAD as in 6.2.11. RAD26 (outbuilding size/height/location) and RAD15 are amenity/aesthetic matters, not alternative provisions - confirm the engine's treatment.

Redcliffe Interim residential precinct: 9.3.1 RAD3 points to Table 9.3.1.3 while the local plan Part K RAD3 points to Table 7.2.1.6.3 (side/rear 1.5 m / 2 m). Which governs dwelling-house building work?
Morayfield South (Emerging community Transition precinct): RAD3 routes it to Table 9.3.1.5, while E3.1 and the Table 9.3.1.6 heading route it to Table 9.3.1.6.
Table 9.3.1.4 heading includes 'Township zone - Residential precinct', but Table 5.7.1 assesses Township residential dwelling houses against the Township zone code (not fetched).
Building heights overlay values come from 2022 council open data, not the Version 8 legal map; lot-specific verification is needed.
Site cover: the definition includes carports, but RAD5 excludes 'patios, balconies and other unenclosed structures'. Decide how to treat open carports.

Not fetched: 6.2.10 Rural zone code (also an alternative-provision code), 6.2.12 Township zone code, 6.2.3 Emerging community zone code, Woodfordia local plan, Planning scheme policy - Residential design.
No swimming pool setback provisions were found in 9.3.1; RR code RAD3 excludes pools and refers to the QDC.
Rural residential: RAD3 (6 m / 4.5 m / 4.5 m) vs RAD48 (6 m road, 1.5-4 m by wall height) - RAD48 is specific to dwelling houses and outbuildings; confirm RAD3 does not also apply.

Rural zone (outside Hamlet): RAD3 setbacks (6m road / 4.5m side / 4.5m rear) expressly exclude 'a dwelling house', and the code has no other boundary setback RAD for a dwelling house, so the accepted-development pathway seems to leave dwelling boundary clearance to the QDC/QHC. Does RAD3 apply to domestic outbuildings, given the Dwelling house definition includes domestic outbuildings? Part B E4.1 (assessable) has no exclusion.

Rural zone: no site cover or roofed-area limit for a dwelling house or outbuildings (unlike Rural residential RAD6). Outbuilding size is unlimited by the zone code; outbuilding height = mapped building height (open data Max 8.5m) except 3.5m in the Hamlet precinct.

Township residential RAD3 rear column says 'Refer to standards in QDC' but Part F E4 says rear 6.0m. Which governs for assessable cases, and how does 'standards in QDC' read after the QHC replaced MP1.2 on 1 Sep 2026?

Township residential: the zone code notes call RAD3 and RAD59(b)(c) 'an alternative provision to the QDC', but Table 1.6.1 (rules 245/246) lists only 6.2.10, 6.2.11 and 9.3.1 as alternative-provision codes; s1.6 rule 248 lists 6.2.12 only as having 'concurrence agency issues'. Is the Building Act s33 status of 6.2.12 provisions effective?
Township residential RAD4 site cover (50%) and RAD1 height have no alternative-provision note, so exceeding them seems to trigger limited code assessment rather than concurrence. Confirm.

Table 5.7.1 rule 4425 editor's-note RAD lists for the Rural zone and Township residential precinct do not match current RAD numbering (e.g. Township list omits RAD59 outbuildings; Rural list omits RAD3/RAD4/RAD39). The Rural MCU table note says '(numbering needs to be checked after changes made)'. The engine should apply the zone code RADs as written.
Building heights overlay values are from 2022 council open data (sampled, not exhaustive), not the Version 8 legal map. Some Rural parcels had no polygon; check each lot.
RAD59 outbuilding roofed-area bands: '600m2 - 1000m2' then '>1000m2 - 2000m2'; E64 header says 'Max. GFA' instead of roofed area. Treated as roofed area per RAD59.
Open carports and site cover: Schedule 1 site cover includes carports, but RAD4 excludes 'other unenclosed structures'.
No swimming pool siting provisions exist in either code; pools appear only as fire-fighting water sources in the bushfire RADs. Pool siting falls to the QDC/QHC and the pool safety standard.
No built-to-boundary provisions in either zone. In Township residential the side minimum (1.5m/2m) applies 'To OMP and wall'.
Dwelling houses in the Township centre/convenience precincts (not listed -> impact assessment) and the Township industry precinct (inconsistent use) have no siting rules; out of scope for the tool.
Rural RAD3 refers to 'not located in a bushfire prone area' and its note to the 'bushfire hazard area'; how this carve-out maps to the Bushfire hazard overlay is not stated.

No 'constrained land', 'Burpengary East' or any other precinct exists for this zone in V8: no child sections under 5.5.8 / 6.2.8 in the eScheme TOC, and ZONE_PREC is always empty in the zone open data. In V8 the Limited development zone is the flood/storm-tide 'extremely unacceptable intolerable risk' zone.

No numeric siting provisions (setbacks, built-to-boundary, site cover, height, outbuilding size, pool setbacks, development footprint, lot-size conditions) exist in 6.2.8. Siting is decided case by case through impact assessment against the whole planning scheme (overlay codes such as 8.2.2 Flood hazard would drive floor levels and siting).
Whether a swimming pool (no GFA) counts as 'minor building work' or a 'new building' under PO1 is not stated; PO1 is in any case only an impact-assessment benchmark.

Existing lawful dwelling houses in the zone: any building work, including a new shed, carport or pool, still needs an impact-assessable application (rule 4428). The tool should flag the lot rather than compute an envelope.
The zone open-data layer has an undocumented field LDZ_DoesNotApply (all 0 for Limited development features).
